issues.body:
Many of the converted scripts run in jobs with a hand-listed non-cone sparse checkout. None of those lists gains scripts/yaml_dependency.py in this diff (no workflow file is touched at all), so the module is simply absent from the working copy at runtime.

Confirmed against the checkout:
- .github/workflows/dispatch.yml:109-113 checks out only scripts/dispatch-tick-floor.py, scripts/ci-latency-alert.py, .github/workflows/dispatch.yml -- then dispatch.yml:143 runs `python3 registry/scripts/dispatch-tick-floor.py --self-test`, whose _load_workflow now does `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml`.
- groom-sweep.yml:396-401 -> :435 metrics-alert.py --self-test (_test_workflow_seam).
- groom-sweep.yml:482-487 -> :524 dispatch-stall-alert.py --self-test (_load_workflow).
- groom-sweep.yml:578-584 -> :603 ci-latency-alert.py --self-test AND :619 the live alert run (module-level import).
- groom-sweep.yml:661-667 -> :690 ratelimit-alert.py --self-test (_test_workflow_seam, line 966 -- the import sits ABOVE the REQUIRED_FILES-missing chk() at line 969, so it cannot even degrade gracefully).
- groom-sweep.yml:754-758 -> :783 groom-mint-alert.py --self-test.
- metrics.yml:192-197 and regate-sweep.yml:69-75 have the same gap.

Every one of those self-test steps is deliberately NOT continue-on-error ("a detector is never trusted to watch anything before it has proved itself on this tick's code"). ModuleNotFoundError is raised before any assertion runs, so the jobs hard-fail. pr-gate uses a full checkout, so this is invisible pre-merge -- the precise live/gate divergence dispatch.yml:100-108 and ratelimit-alert.py:71-73 warn about.
issues.fix_hint: Add `scripts/yaml_dependency.py` to every sparse-checkout block whose job executes a converted script: dispatch.yml:109, groom-sweep.yml:396, :482, :578, :661, :754, metrics.yml:192, regate-sweep.yml:69 (and audit dispatch.yml:1581 for worker-pr.py --self-test). Also add it to the REQUIRED_FILES tuples that mirror those blocks (ratelimit-alert.py:74, ci-latency-alert.py:111, and the equivalents in dispatch-tick-floor.py / dispatch-stall-alert.py / groom-mint-alert.py) so the existing both-directions seam assertion pins it. The alternative -- keeping the helper dependency-free by inlining it -- defeats the point; enrolling the file is the right fix.
issues.title: New shared module is not in any sparse-checkout; six watchdog lanes and the dispatch tick-floor gate will fail with ModuleNotFoundError('yaml_dependency')

issues.body:
The guard at lines 97-102 previously wrapped `import yaml` in `except ImportError`, setting yaml=None and stashing _YAML_IMPORT_ERROR so the two AlarmError sites (lines 471, 1082) could report "PyYAML unavailable" as a controlled detector failure. The diff replaces the body with two statements and narrows the handler to RuntimeError. Two escape paths are now uncaught at module import time:

1. `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` raises ModuleNotFoundError (an ImportError, not a RuntimeError) whenever scripts/yaml_dependency.py is absent -- which is the case under groom-sweep.yml:578-584 and dispatch.yml:109-113 and regate-sweep.yml:69-75. This kills the module before ALALARM handling exists, taking out both the self-test step (groom-sweep.yml:603) and the live alert run (:619).
2. require_yaml deliberately re-raises the nested ModuleNotFoundError un-wrapped when exc.name != 'yaml' (yaml_dependency.py:20-21) -- e.g. a broken/partial PyYAML install. That is also an ImportError, so it is no longer caught either; the previous code converted it into the AlarmError path.

The handler is marked `# pragma: no cover - fail loud rather than skip M1`, but "fail loud" here meant a structured AlarmError, not an unhandled traceback at import.
issues.fix_hint: Catch both families -- `except (ImportError, RuntimeError) as _exc:` -- so the module-level guard still degrades to yaml=None/_YAML_IMPORT_ERROR for a missing helper file or a broken PyYAML, and let the AlarmError sites at lines 471/1082 keep reporting the cause. (Still required even after yaml_dependency.py is added to the sparse checkouts, since that guard exists precisely to survive an incomplete environment.) Alternatively, have require_yaml wrap the nested ModuleNotFoundError in PyYAMLUnavailable-with-cause rather than re-raising it bare, so a single RuntimeError catch is sufficient.
issues.title: Narrowing `except ImportError` to `except RuntimeError` around a module-level import turns a graceful degradation into an uncaught crash

issues.body:
This file documents the repo's own guard against exactly this failure: REQUIRED_FILES (line 74) is asserted present at runtime (line 969) AND asserted line-by-line against the live sparse-checkout block (lines 1060-1064), with a _test_harness that proves the missing-input path reds rather than skipping (lines 1084-1090). The same pattern exists in ci-latency-alert.py and dispatch-tick-floor.py.

This PR adds a hard file dependency to 15+ scripts and extends none of these tuples, so nothing in the suite can observe the divergence. Worse, the import at line 966 executes BEFORE the REQUIRED_FILES check at line 969, so even if yaml_dependency.py were added to REQUIRED_FILES, the module import would still crash first instead of producing the intended named chk() failure.

The one new assertion the PR does add (worker-live.sh:4123) only proves the preflight ERE still classifies a `from yaml_dependency import` line as a PyYAML consumer. That is a correct check but it is orthogonal: it says nothing about whether the helper FILE is present in a sparse checkout. As written the PR ships a new trust-plane dependency with zero coverage of its own delivery.
issues.fix_hint: Add "scripts/yaml_dependency.py" to REQUIRED_FILES here and in the sibling scripts, and move the `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` call BELOW the REQUIRED_FILES-missing chk() (or import it lazily inside the parse helper) so an incomplete checkout produces the named seam failure instead of a traceback. Consider one shared assertion -- e.g. in worker-live.sh or a new seam check -- that scans the suite for `from yaml_dependency import` and requires every sparse-checkout block hosting such a script to name scripts/yaml_dependency.py on its own line, so the next converted script cannot re-open the gap.
issues.title: No seam assertion pins the new cross-file dependency, so the sparse-checkout drift this PR creates is undetectable in pr-gate

issues.body:
All three rows inject a fake `importer` (lines 33, 40, 53). The production default -- `importer=importlib.import_module` bound at def time, called with the literal string "yaml" -- is never executed. A regression that changed the default to the wrong module name, or that made the default a no-op, would leave this self-test fully green while every caller in the repo broke. Given that the whole point of this module is to be the single chokepoint for ~20 workflow-seam parsers, its own self-test should cover the un-injected path.

The three injected rows themselves are genuine (each flips red on a wrong answer) -- this is a coverage gap, not a vacuous test.
issues.fix_hint: Add a row that calls `require_yaml()` with no importer override and asserts the result is the same object as a direct `importlib.import_module("yaml")` -- guarded so a genuinely PyYAML-less environment reports the expected PyYAMLUnavailable rather than a spurious FAIL. That pins both the module name and the default binding.
issues.title: self_test never exercises the DEFAULT importer, so the real code path is untested

issues.body: Line 69: `if "--self-test" in sys.argv and sys.argv[1:] == ["--self-test"]:`. The second conjunct strictly implies the first, so the membership test is dead. Also note the equality form means the script exits with the usage string (non-zero) if a runner ever passes an extra flag alongside --self-test; that is a defensible fail-closed choice, but it is stricter than the sibling scripts in the suite.
issues.title: Redundant conjunct in the __main__ argv guard

verdict.summary: The refactor is a good idea (one actionable, fail-closed PyYAML loader instead of ~20 bare `import yaml` sites) and the new helper's own self-test is non-vacuous. But it introduces a NEW hard cross-file dependency -- scripts/yaml_dependency.py -- into 15+ scripts without enrolling that file in ANY of the sparse-checkout blocks or REQUIRED_FILES tuples those scripts run under. Verified in the checkout: .github/workflows/dispatch.yml:109-113 (dispatch-tick-floor), groom-sweep.yml:396-401 (metrics-alert), :482-487 (dispatch-stall-alert), :578-584 (ci-latency), :661-667 (ratelimit-alert), :754-758 (groom-mint-alert), metrics.yml:192-197, regate-sweep.yml:69-75 all sparse-check-out a hand-listed set of scripts that does NOT include yaml_dependency.py. Each of those jobs then runs `--self-test` NOT under continue-on-error (dispatch.yml:143, groom-sweep.yml:435, :524, :603, :690, :783). Under those checkouts `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` raises ModuleNotFoundError('yaml_dependency'), so six production watchdog lanes plus the dispatch tick-floor admission gate go red on every tick. ci-latency-alert.py is worse still: the import is at MODULE level and the except clause was narrowed from ImportError to RuntimeError, so the crash is uncaught and the live alert path (groom-sweep.yml:619) dies too. Crucially pr-gate has a FULL checkout, so all of this stays GREEN in the gate and only breaks after merge -- exactly the silent live/gate divergence the REQUIRED_FILES `KEEP IN SYNC` comments (dispatch.yml:100-108, ratelimit-alert.py:71-73) exist to prevent. No new seam assertion was added to catch it, and the worker-live.sh preflight only proves the ERE still classifies the helper as a PyYAML consumer -- it says nothing about the file being present.
